Notation.binderRules.doc:
Binder patterns (the `binders` variant): chains of ∃ and ∀ folded into
one list, an implication, a λ, a function taken by a binder pattern, and an
operator with `assoc := none`.

views.math: \LeanMath{(\exists a,\ \exists b,\ a = b) \wedge (\forall a : \mathbb{N},\ \forall b : \mathbb{N},\ a = a \implies b = b \implies p) \wedge \LeanMathConst{bigsum}\,(\lambda k.\,k + 1) = \LeanMathConst{bigsum}\,f \LeanBreak \wedge (\lambda n.\,n)\,1 = 1 \wedge (p \wedge p) \wedge \neg (\exists c,\ c = c \wedge \neg p \wedge (\forall a_{1} : \mathbb{N},\ a_{1} = a_{1}))}
views.math:binders: \LeanMath{(\exists a, b.\, a = b) \wedge ((\forall a, b.\, a = a \Rightarrow b = b \Rightarrow p) \wedge (\sum_{k} k + 1 \LeanBreak = \sum f \wedge ((n \mapsto n)\,1 = 1 \wedge ((p \wedge p) \wedge \neg(\exists c.\, c = c \wedge (\neg p \wedge (\forall a_{1}.\, a_{1} = a_{1})))))))}
views.math:named: \LeanMath{(\exists a,\ \exists b,\ a = b) \wedge (\forall a : \mathbb{N},\ \forall b : \mathbb{N},\ a = a \implies b = b \implies p) \wedge \LeanMathConst{bigsum}\,(\lambda k.\,k + 1) = \LeanMathConst{bigsum}\,f \LeanBreak \wedge (\lambda n.\,n)\,1 = 1 \wedge (p \wedge p) \wedge \neg (\exists c,\ c = c \wedge \neg p \wedge (\forall a_{1} : \mathbb{N},\ a_{1} = a_{1}))}
views.prose: \LeanProse{Let $f \in \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and $p$ be a proposition. Then (1)~$\exists a,\ \exists b,\ a = b$, (2)~$\forall a : \mathbb{N},\ \forall b : \mathbb{N},\ a = a \implies b = b \implies p$, (3)~$\LeanMathConst{bigsum}\,(\lambda k.\,k + 1) = \LeanMathConst{bigsum}\,f$, (4)~$(\lambda n.\,n)\,1 = 1$, (5)~$p \wedge p$ and (6)~$\neg (\exists c,\ c = c \wedge \neg p \wedge (\forall a_{1} : \mathbb{N},\ a_{1} = a_{1}))$.}

Notation.binders.doc:
Binders: bounded quantifiers, ∃, implication, function types, λ, an
applied variable, and a `match`, which falls back to Lean's printer.

views.prose: \LeanProse{Let $a, b, c, d, e, f, g \in \mathbb{N}$. Assume $a + b + c + d = e + f + g$, $e + f + g = a + b + c + d$ and $a \cdot b \cdot c \cdot d = e \cdot f \cdot g$. Then (1)~$a + b + c + d + e + f + g = e + f + g + a + b + c + d$, (2)~$a + b + c = c + b + a$, (3)~$c + d + e = e + d + c$ and (4)~$a \cdot b \cdot c \cdot d \cdot e = e \cdot d \cdot c \cdot b \cdot a$.}

Assume $2n = m$, $\neg \LeanMathConst{Realize}\,n\,m\,\rho$, $\lub{n, m, k, n} = k$ and $\mathbf{0} = 0$. Then (1)~$n \mathbin{\triangleright} (m \mathbin{\triangleright} k) = n \mathbin{\triangleright} m \mathbin{\triangleright} k$, (2)~$\vdash L$ and (3)~$n = m \implies n \models m$.}
